proposed.label: Choosing the wrong one of the two sides that form theta as the hypotenuse
proposed.description: Two sides touch the angle theta, the hypotenuse and the adjacent leg. The student picks the leg as the hypotenuse instead of the side across from the right angle, and so calls the true hypotenuse the adjacent side.

proposed.label: Swapping the opposite and adjacent sides
proposed.description: The student finds the hypotenuse correctly but gives the name opposite to the leg that touches the angle theta and the name adjacent to the leg that lies across from theta.

proposed.label: Mixing up the two meanings of opposite
proposed.description: The student calls the side across from the right angle (the hypotenuse) the opposite side, and then names the side across from theta as the hypotenuse, confusing opposite the right angle with opposite theta.

proposed.label: Mixing up the two meanings of opposite
proposed.description: The student calls the side across from the right angle (the hypotenuse) the opposite side, and then names the side across from theta as the hypotenuse, confusing opposite the right angle with opposite theta.

proposed.label: Choosing the wrong one of the two sides that form theta as the hypotenuse

proposed.label: Drops the 90 degrees minus from a complementary-angle statement
proposed.description: The student sees sin squared plus cos squared and takes the Pythagorean identity to hold, writing cos^2 y where the true statement needs cos^2(90 - y). They do not substitute both angles, so they never see that the two squared terms are not for the same angle.

proposed.label: Thinks the sine of the complement equals the sine of the angle
proposed.description: The student treats 90 degrees minus x as if it changed nothing, so they accept sin(90 - x) = sin x without evaluating either side. The calculator shows sin(90 - x) equals cos x, which is not sin x unless x is 45 degrees.

proposed.label: Gives the ratio itself instead of its reciprocal
proposed.description: The student finds x over r correctly but writes it as sec, the value of cos, instead of turning the fraction over to get r over x.
